96	def compile_matchers(matchers):
97	    """Validate ``matchers`` and return ``(key, op, value, pattern)`` tuples.
98	
99	    Each element is an object with exactly ``key`` (non-empty string), ``op``
100	    (one of ``=``, ``!=``, ``=~``, ``!~``) and ``value`` (string, possibly
101	    empty). ``None`` and an empty list add no condition; regex patterns are
102	    compiled here, so an invalid pattern is rejected before any series is read.
103	    """
104	    if matchers is None:
105	        return ()
106	    if not isinstance(matchers, (list, tuple)):
107	        raise ObsError("matchers must be a list of matcher objects")
108	    compiled = []
109	    for element in matchers:
110	        if not isinstance(element, dict):
111	            raise ObsError("each matcher must be an object with key, op and value")
112	        if set(element) != {"key", "op", "value"}:
113	            raise ObsError("each matcher must contain exactly key, op and value")
114	        key, op, value = element["key"], element["op"], element["value"]
115	        if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
116	            raise ObsError("matcher key must be a non-empty string")
117	        if op not in MATCHER_OPS:
118	            raise ObsError("matcher op must be one of %s" % (MATCHER_OPS,))
119	        if not isinstance(value, str):
120	            raise ObsError("matcher value must be a string")
121	        pattern = None
122	        if op in ("=~", "!~"):
123	            try:
124	                pattern = re.compile(value)
125	            except re.error as exc:
126	                raise ObsError("invalid matcher regex %r: %s" % (value, exc))
127	        compiled.append((key, op, value, pattern))
128	    return tuple(compiled)
129

131	def matchers_hold(series_labels, compiled):
132	    """True when every compiled matcher holds for ``series_labels``.
133	
134	    A missing key never satisfies ``=``/``=~`` but always satisfies ``!=``/
135	    ``!~``; regex matchers anchor with ``fullmatch`` so the pattern covers the
136	    whole value. Only real labels are considered.
137	    """
138	    for key, op, value, pattern in compiled:
139	        present = key in series_labels
140	        if op == "=":
141	            if not present or series_labels[key] != value:
142	                return False
143	        elif op == "!=":
144	            if present and series_labels[key] == value:
145	                return False
146	        elif op == "=~":
147	            if not present or pattern.fullmatch(series_labels[key]) is None:
148	                return False
149	        else:  # "!~"
150	            if present and pattern.fullmatch(series_labels[key]) is not None:
151	                return False
152	    return True

155	def parse_matchers_text(text, field="matchers"):
156	    """Decode a JSON array text of matcher objects; ``None``/absent adds none.
157	
158	    Used by the HTTP and CLI entry points, where the parameter arrives as a
159	    string. Returns the raw decoded list (validated later by
160	    :func:`compile_matchers`, which runs even with no candidate series). Empty
161	    text and an explicit JSON ``null`` are illegal here (unlike omitting the
162	    parameter or passing Python ``None`` to ``query``).
163	    """
164	    if text is None:
165	        return None
166	    if not isinstance(text, str) or not text:
167	        raise ObsError("%s must be a JSON array of matcher objects" % field)
168	    try:
169	        data = json.loads(text)
170	    except ValueError:
171	        raise ObsError("%s must be a JSON array of matcher objects" % field)
172	    if data is None:
173	        raise ObsError("%s must be a JSON array of matcher objects" % field)
174	    if not isinstance(data, list):
175	        raise ObsError("%s must be a JSON array of matcher objects" % field)
176	    return data

179	def _clean_samples(samples, now):
180	    """Validate ``samples`` against the optional clock; return clean pairs.
181	
182	    Shared by ``SeriesStore.write`` and ``SeriesStore.write_batch`` so single
183	    and multi-series writes apply exactly the same sample rules.
184	    """
185	    if not isinstance(samples, (list, tuple)):
186	        raise ObsError("samples must be a list of [timestamp_ms, value] pairs")
187	    clean = []
188	    for entry in samples:
189	        if not isinstance(entry, (list, tuple)) or len(entry) != 2:
190	            raise ObsError("each sample must be a [timestamp_ms, value] pair")
191	        stamp, value = entry
192	        if not _num(stamp) or not _num(value):
193	            raise ObsError("sample timestamp and value must be numbers")
194	        if now is not None and int(stamp) > int(now):
195	            raise ObsError("sample timestamp %d is in the future (now=%d)"
196	                           % (int(stamp), int(now)))
197	        clean.append((int(stamp), float(value)))
198	    if not clean:
199	        raise ObsError("samples must not be empty")
200	    return clean

203	def _aggregate(values, agg):
204	    if agg == "sum":
205	        return float(sum(values))
206	    if agg == "avg":
207	        return sum(values) / float(len(values))
208	    if agg == "min":
209	        return float(min(values))
210	    if agg == "max":
211	        return float(max(values))
212	    if agg == "count":
213	        return len(values)

217	def _atomic_write(path, text):
218	    """Write ``text`` to ``path`` through a temp file plus os.replace."""
219	    directory = os.path.dirname(path)
220	    if directory:
221	        os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
222	    with open(path + ".tmp", "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
223	        handle.write(text)
224	        handle.flush()
225	        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
226	    os.replace(path + ".tmp", path)

230	    return json.dumps({"t": stamp, "v": value}, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"

234	    """Canonical UTF-8 bytes of a snapshot document for its SHA-256 digest."""

236	                      separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")

239	class SeriesStore:
240	    """Append-mostly time series store persisted under ``root``.
241	
242	    Layout::
243	
244	        <root>/series.json                 registry: series_id -> series row
245	        <root>/points/<series_id>.jsonl    one ``{"t":ts,"v":value}`` per line
246	        <root>/quotas.json                 tenant -> {"max_series", "max_points"}
247	        <root>/retention.json              tenant -> {"retention_ms"}
248	    """
249	
250	    def __init__(self, root):
251	        if not isinstance(root, (str, os.PathLike)) or not str(root):
252	            raise ObsError("root must be a non-empty path")
253	        self.root = os.path.abspath(str(root))
254	        self.points_dir = os.path.join(self.root, "points")
255	        self.series_path = os.path.join(self.root, "series.json")
256	        self.quota_path = os.path.join(self.root, "quotas.json")
257	        self.retention_path = os.path.join(self.root, "retention.json")
258	        self.revision_path = os.path.join(self.root, "revision.json")
259	        self._lock = threading.RLock()
260	        self._series, self._samples, self._writes = {}, {}, 0
261	        self._quotas = {}
262	        self._retention = {}
263	        self._revision = 0
264	        self._secret = None
265	        os.makedirs(self.points_dir, exist_ok=True)
266	        self._load()
267	        self._load_quotas()
268	        self._load_retention()
269	        self._load_revision()
270	
271	    def _points_path(self, sid):
272	        return os.path.join(self.points_dir, sid + ".jsonl")
273	
274	    # ------------------------------------------------------------- persistence
275	    def _load(self):
276	        rows = []
277	        if os.path.exists(self.series_path):
278	            try:
279	                with open(self.series_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
280	                    rows = json.load(handle)
281	            except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
282	                raise ObsError("cannot read series registry: %s" % exc)
283	        for row in rows:
284	            sid = row.get("series_id")
285	            if not sid:
286	                continue
287	            self._series[sid] = {"series_id": sid, "tenant": row.get("tenant"),
288	                                 "metric": row.get("metric"),
289	                                 "labels": [[str(k), str(v)] for k, v in row.get("labels", [])],
290	                                 "identity": row.get("identity")}
291	            self._samples[sid] = self._read_points(sid)
292	
293	    def _read_points(self, sid):
294	        """Reload one point file, skipping unreadable lines.
295	
296	        Repeated lines for the same timestamp (left behind by historical
297	        overwrites) collapse to the last value stored, so occupancy counts each
298	        distinct timestamp once after a reopen.
299	        """
300	        rows = {}
301	        path = self._points_path(sid)
302	        if os.path.exists(path):
303	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
304	                for line in handle:
305	                    try:
306	                        row = json.loads(line)
307	                        rows[int(row["t"])] = float(row["v"])
308	                    except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
309	                        continue
310	        return sorted(rows.items())
311	
312	    def _save_registry(self):
313	        _atomic_write(self.series_path, json.dumps(
314	            [self._series[sid] for sid in sorted(self._series)],
315	            sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")))
316	
317	    def _rewrite_points(self, sid):
318	        _atomic_write(self._points_path(sid),
319	                      "".join(_line(ts, value) for ts, value in self._samples[sid]))
320	
321	    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- revision
322	    # The store keeps one persistent, monotonically increasing revision.
323	    # Every successful commit that changes samples or the visible scope (a
324	    # single write, a batch, a snapshot replay or a retention run that
325	    # actually drops samples) increases it exactly once; pure duplicates,
326	    # dry runs, validation failures, conflicts, quota rejections and
327	    # no-op retention runs leave it untouched, as do all reads.
328	    def _load_revision(self):
329	        """Reload ``revision.json``; a missing file means revision 0."""
330	        if not os.path.exists(self.revision_path):
331	            return
332	        try:
333	            with open(self.revision_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
334	                data = json.load(handle)
335	        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
336	            raise ObsError("cannot read revision state: %s" % exc)
337	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
338	            raise ObsError("cannot read revision state: root must be an object")
339	        revision = data.get("revision", 0)
340	        if isinstance(revision, bool) or not isinstance(revision, int) or revision < 0:
341	            raise ObsError("cannot read revision state: malformed revision")
342	        secret = data.get("secret")
343	        if secret is not None and not isinstance(secret, str):
344	            raise ObsError("cannot read revision state: malformed secret")
345	        self._revision = revision
346	        self._secret = secret
347	
348	    def _save_revision(self):
349	        _atomic_write(self.revision_path, json.dumps(
350	            {"revision": self._revision, "secret": self._secret},
351	            sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")))
352	
353	    def _disk_revision(self):
354	        """The revision persisted on disk (0 when missing or unreadable)."""
355	        try:
356	            with open(self.revision_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
357	                data = json.load(handle)
358	            revision = data.get("revision", 0) if isinstance(data, dict) else 0
359	            if isinstance(revision, int) and not isinstance(revision, bool) \
360	                    and revision >= 0:
361	                return revision
362	        except (OSError, ValueError):
363	            pass
364	        return 0
365	
366	    def _refresh_revision(self):
367	        """Fold in commits another instance of this data dir may have persisted."""
368	        disk = self._disk_revision()
369	        if disk > self._revision:
370	            self._revision = disk
371	
372	    def _bump_revision(self):
373	        """Advance the persistent revision by one; call only inside a commit."""
374	        self._refresh_revision()
375	        self._revision += 1
376	        self._save_revision()
377	        return self._revision
378	
379	    def _revision_now(self):
380	        """The current revision, folding in other instances' commits."""
381	        with self._lock:
382	            self._refresh_revision()
383	            return self._revision
384	
385	    def _ensure_secret(self):
386	        """Mint and persist the token-signing secret on first use.
387	
388	        The persisted state is re-read first so a second instance of the same
389	        data dir adopts the existing secret and revision instead of
390	        clobbering them.
391	        """
392	        if self._secret is not None:
393	            return
394	        try:
395	            with open(self.revision_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
396	                data = json.load(handle)
397	        except (OSError, ValueError):
398	            data = None
399	        if isinstance(data, dict):
400	            revision = data.get("revision")
401	            if isinstance(revision, int) and not isinstance(revision, bool) \
402	                    and revision > self._revision:
403	                self._revision = revision
404	            secret = data.get("secret")
405	            if isinstance(secret, str) and secret:
406	                self._secret = secret
407	                return
408	        self._secret = secrets.token_hex(32)
409	        self._save_revision()
410	
411	    # ------------------------------------------------------------- consistency
412	    def consistency_token(self, tenant):
413	        """A read-consistency token binding ``tenant`` to the current revision.
414	
415	        The token is an HMAC-signed ``{"tenant", "revision", "v"}`` payload;
416	        the signing secret is persisted in ``revision.json``, so tokens stay
417	        verifiable after a restart and across instances sharing the data dir.
418	        """
419	        tenant = self._clean_tenant(tenant)
420	        with self._lock:
421	            self._ensure_secret()
422	            self._refresh_revision()
423	            revision = self._revision
424	            payload = json.dumps({"revision": revision, "tenant": tenant, "v": 1},
425	                                 sort_keys=True,
426	                                 separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
427	            body = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(payload).decode("ascii").rstrip("=")
428	            signature = hmac.new(self._secret.encode("ascii"), body.encode("ascii"),
429	                                 hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
430	            token = "%s.%s.%s" % (TOKEN_PREFIX, body, signature)
431	        return {"tenant": tenant, "token": token, "revision": revision}
432	
433	    def check_read_token(self, token, tenant):
434	        """Validate ``token`` for reading ``tenant``; return its revision.
435	
436	        A tampered, malformed, foreign-secret or cross-tenant token raises
437	        ``ObsError("invalid read token")`` (``400`` semantics); a token whose
438	        revision this instance has not reached yet raises
439	        ``ObsError("read revision unavailable")`` (``409`` semantics).
440	        """
441	        if not isinstance(token, str) or not token:
442	            raise ObsError("invalid read token")
443	        parts = token.split(".")
444	        if len(parts) != 3 or parts[0] != TOKEN_PREFIX \
445	                or not parts[1] or not parts[2]:
446	            raise ObsError("invalid read token")
447	        body, signature = parts[1], parts[2]
448	        with self._lock:
449	            self._ensure_secret()
450	            secret = self._secret
451	        expected = hmac.new(secret.encode("ascii"), body.encode("ascii"),
452	                            hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
453	        if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature):
454	            raise ObsError("invalid read token")
455	        try:
456	            padding = "=" * (-len(body) % 4)
457	            payload = json.loads(
458	                base64.urlsafe_b64decode(body + padding).decode("utf-8"))
459	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
460	            raise ObsError("invalid read token")
461	        if not isinstance(payload, dict) or payload.get("v") != 1:
462	            raise ObsError("invalid read token")
463	        token_tenant = payload.get("tenant")
464	        revision = payload.get("revision")
465	        if not isinstance(token_tenant, str) or not token_tenant \
466	                or isinstance(revision, bool) or not isinstance(revision, int) \
467	                or revision < 0:
468	            raise ObsError("invalid read token")
469	        if not isinstance(tenant, str) or token_tenant != tenant:
470	            raise ObsError("invalid read token")
471	        with self._lock:
472	            self._refresh_revision()
473	            current = self._revision
474	        if revision > current:
475	            raise ObsError("read revision unavailable")
476	        return revision

478	    @staticmethod
479	    def _clean_return_revision(return_revision):
480	        """``return_revision`` must be a real boolean (an explicit null is
481	        rejected, not treated as ``False``); checked before any state change."""
482	        if not isinstance(return_revision, bool):
483	            raise ObsError("return_revision must be a boolean")

486	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ quotas
487	    def _load_quotas(self):
488	        """Reload ``quotas.json``; a missing file means every tenant is unlimited."""
489	        if not os.path.exists(self.quota_path):
490	            return
491	        try:
492	            with open(self.quota_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
493	                data = json.load(handle)
494	        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
495	            raise ObsError("cannot read quota config: %s" % exc)
496	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
497	            raise ObsError("cannot read quota config: root must be an object")
498	        for tenant, row in data.items():
499	            if not isinstance(tenant, str) or not tenant or not isinstance(row, dict):
500	                raise ObsError("cannot read quota config: malformed entry")
501	            self._quotas[tenant] = {
502	                "max_series": self._clean_limit(row.get("max_series"), "max_series"),
503	                "max_points": self._clean_limit(row.get("max_points"), "max_points")}

505	    @staticmethod
506	    def _clean_limit(value, field):
507	        """A limit is a non-negative integer or ``None`` (unlimited)."""
508	        if value is None:
509	            return None
510	        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
511	            raise ObsError("%s must be a non-negative integer or null" % field)
512	        if value < 0:
513	            raise ObsError("%s must be a non-negative integer or null" % field)
514	        return value

516	    @staticmethod
517	    def _clean_tenant(tenant):
518	        if not isinstance(tenant, str) or not tenant:
519	            raise ObsError("tenant must be a non-empty string")
520	        return tenant

522	    def _save_quotas(self):
523	        _atomic_write(self.quota_path, json.dumps(
524	            {tenant: self._quotas[tenant] for tenant in sorted(self._quotas)},
525	            sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")))

527	    def set_quota(self, tenant, max_series, max_points):
528	        """Configure the per-tenant limits; ``None`` means unlimited.
529	
530	        Limits may be lowered below current usage; pure duplicate/overwrite
531	        writes stay allowed afterwards. Configuring a quota never creates a
532	        series.
533	        """
534	        tenant = self._clean_tenant(tenant)
535	        max_series = self._clean_limit(max_series, "max_series")
536	        max_points = self._clean_limit(max_points, "max_points")
537	        with self._lock:
538	            self._quotas[tenant] = {"max_series": max_series, "max_points": max_points}
539	            self._save_quotas()
540	            return self.get_quota(tenant)

542	    def get_quota(self, tenant):
543	        """Return limits and current usage for ``tenant`` in one snapshot."""
544	        tenant = self._clean_tenant(tenant)
545	        with self._lock:
546	            limits = self._quotas.get(tenant, {"max_series": None, "max_points": None})
547	            series = points = 0
548	            for sid, row in self._series.items():
549	                if row["tenant"] == tenant:
550	                    series += 1
551	                    points += len(self._samples[sid])
552	            return {"tenant": tenant, "max_series": limits["max_series"],
553	                    "max_points": limits["max_points"], "series": series, "points": points}

555	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------- write
556	    def write(self, tenant, metric, labels, samples, now=None, overwrite=False,
557	              return_revision=False):
558	        """Store ``samples`` = ``[(timestamp_ms, value), ...]``.
559	
560	        Idempotent: an identical ``(series, timestamp)`` value is a duplicate
561	        and changes nothing. A differing value for a stored timestamp raises
562	        ``ObsError`` unless ``overwrite=True``.
563	
564	        ``now`` is ``None`` (no future check) or a non-boolean integer;
565	        ``overwrite`` and ``return_revision`` must be booleans. Anything else
566	        raises ``ObsError`` before any validation or state change: no series,
567	        points, write counter, quota usage, revision or temp file is touched.
568	
569	        The whole batch is checked against the tenant's configured quotas
570	        *after* input validation and conflict rules, using the net new series
571	        and distinct new timestamps the batch would add (same-value replays,
572	        overwrites and timestamps repeated inside the batch add nothing). A
573	        batch that would exceed either limit is rejected wholesale with
574	        ``ObsError``: no series, points or write counter change is kept.
575	
576	        A write that stores anything increases the persistent revision by
577	        one; a pure-duplicate write does not. With ``return_revision=True``
578	        the result carries ``revision``: the commit revision when something
579	        was written, otherwise the current revision.
580	        """
581	        if now is not None and (isinstance(now, bool) or not isinstance(now, int)):
582	            raise ObsError("now must be a non-boolean integer timestamp in ms or None")
583	        if not isinstance(overwrite, bool):
584	            raise ObsError("overwrite must be a boolean")
585	        self._clean_return_revision(return_revision)
586	        clean = _clean_samples(samples, now)
587	        # Labels/tenant are validated before the lock so conflicts and quota
588	        # breaches never surface as identity errors.
589	        pairs = _labels_list(labels)
590	        identity = canonical_identity(tenant, metric, pairs)
591	        sid = hashlib.sha256(identity.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
592	        revision = None
593	        with self._lock:
594	            existed = sid in self._series
595	            current = dict(self._samples.get(sid, ()))
596	            merged = dict(current)
597	            written = duplicates = 0
598	            new_stamps = set()
599	            overwritten = False
600	            for stamp, value in clean:
601	                if stamp in merged:
602	                    if merged[stamp] != value:
603	                        if not overwrite:
604	                            raise ObsError(
605	                                "conflict for %s at timestamp %d: stored=%r incoming=%r"
606	                                % (sid, stamp, merged[stamp], value))
607	                        if stamp in current:
608	                            overwritten = True
609	                    else:
610	                        duplicates += 1
611	                        continue
612	                else:
613	                    new_stamps.add(stamp)
614	                merged[stamp] = value
615	                written += 1
616	
617	            quota = self._quotas.get(tenant)
618	            if quota is not None:
619	                used_series = used_points = 0
620	                for sid_, row in self._series.items():
621	                    if row["tenant"] == tenant:
622	                        used_series += 1
623	                        used_points += len(self._samples[sid_])
624	                new_series = 0 if existed else 1
625	                new_points = len(new_stamps)
626	                limit_series = quota["max_series"]
627	                limit_points = quota["max_points"]
628	                if new_series and limit_series is not None \
629	                        and used_series + new_series > limit_series:
630	                    raise ObsError(
631	                        "quota exceeded for tenant %r: series %d+%d > max_series %s"
632	                        % (tenant, used_series, new_series, limit_series))
633	                if new_points and limit_points is not None \
634	                        and used_points + new_points > limit_points:
635	                    raise ObsError(
636	                        "quota exceeded for tenant %r: points %d+%d > max_points %s"
637	                        % (tenant, used_points, new_points, limit_points))
638	
639	            if not existed:
640	                self._series[sid] = {"series_id": sid, "tenant": tenant, "metric": metric,
641	                                     "labels": pairs, "identity": identity}
642	                self._samples[sid] = []
643	            if written:
644	                self._samples[sid] = sorted(merged.items())
645	                if overwritten:
646	                    # An overwrite replaced a stored value: rewrite the file so a
647	                    # timestamp never occupies more than one physical line.
648	                    self._rewrite_points(sid)
649	                else:
650	                    fresh = sorted((stamp, merged[stamp]) for stamp in new_stamps)
651	                    with open(self._points_path(sid), "a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
652	                        handle.write("".join(_line(ts, value) for ts, value in fresh))
653	                        handle.flush()
654	                        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
655	                self._writes += 1
656	                revision = self._bump_revision()
657	                self._save_registry()
658	        result = {"series_id": sid, "written": written, "duplicates": duplicates}
659	        if return_revision:
660	            result["revision"] = revision if revision is not None \
661	                else self._revision_now()
662	        return result

664	    def write_batch(self, entries, now=None, overwrite=False, return_revision=False):
665	        """Atomically store many series' samples in one all-or-nothing batch.
666	
667	        ``entries`` is a non-empty list of objects, each with exactly the
668	        required fields ``tenant``, ``metric`` and ``samples`` plus an optional
669	        ``labels`` (omitted means ``{}``); identity and sample validation are
670	        the same as :meth:`write`. Entries may span tenants and metrics and
671	        may repeat a series. ``now`` is ``None`` (no future check) or a
672	        non-boolean integer; ``overwrite`` must be a boolean.
673	
674	        The whole batch is validated before any conflict is reported, and all
675	        conflicts before any quota check. Entries and their samples are then
676	        applied in input order, so a later entry sees the earlier entries of
677	        the same batch: a same-value restatement counts as a duplicate, a
678	        differing value conflicts unless ``overwrite`` (then it replaces and
679	        counts as written). Quotas are charged per tenant with the batch's net
680	        new series and distinct new timestamps — duplicates and overwrites add
681	        no occupancy, and only dimensions that actually increase are checked.
682	
683	        Any rejection (structure, validation, future sample, conflict, quota)
684	        raises ``ObsError`` and leaves no series, sample, write-count or
685	        revision change behind, on disk included. On success
686	        ``stats()["writes"]`` and the persistent revision each increase by
687	        exactly one when the batch wrote anything; a pure-duplicate batch
688	        increases nothing. Returns ``{"written", "duplicates", "results"}``
689	        where ``results`` holds one ``{"series_id", "written", "duplicates"}``
690	        per entry, in input order, and the totals are their sums. With
691	        ``return_revision=True`` (a boolean; anything else is rejected before
692	        any validation) the result also carries ``revision``: the commit
693	        revision, or the current revision when nothing was committed.
694	        """
695	        return self._apply_batch(entries, now=now, overwrite=overwrite,
696	                                 commit=True, return_revision=return_revision)
697	
698	    def _apply_batch(self, entries, now=None, overwrite=False, commit=True,
699	                     return_revision=False):
700	        """The ``write_batch`` machinery; ``commit=False`` only validates and counts.
701	
702	        With ``commit=False`` every check runs exactly as for a real batch
703	        (structure, samples, future timestamps, conflicts, quotas) and the
704	        same ``{"written", "duplicates", "results"}`` preview is returned, but
705	        no series, sample, counter or file ever changes. Used by snapshot
706	        replay, where a dry run must prove applicable without applying.
707	        """
708	        if now is not None and (isinstance(now, bool) or not isinstance(now, int)):
709	            raise ObsError("now must be a non-boolean integer timestamp in ms or None")
710	        if not isinstance(overwrite, bool):
711	            raise ObsError("overwrite must be a boolean")
712	        self._clean_return_revision(return_revision)
713	        if not isinstance(entries, (list, tuple)) or not entries:
714	            raise ObsError("entries must be a non-empty list of entry objects")
715	        # Phase 1: validate every entry before any conflict or quota check, so
716	        # a malformed later entry never masks an earlier conflict.
717	        prepared = []
718	        for index, entry in enumerate(entries):
719	            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
720	                raise ObsError("entry %d must be an object with tenant, metric "
721	                               "and samples" % index)
722	            if set(entry) - {"tenant", "metric", "samples", "labels"}:
723	                raise ObsError("entry %d must contain only tenant, metric, "
724	                               "samples and labels" % index)
725	            for field in ("tenant", "metric", "samples"):
726	                if entry.get(field) is None:
727	                    raise ObsError("entry %d: missing field: %s" % (index, field))
728	            clean = _clean_samples(entry["samples"], now)
729	            pairs = _labels_list(entry.get("labels"))
730	            identity = canonical_identity(entry["tenant"], entry["metric"], pairs)
731	            sid = hashlib.sha256(identity.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
732	            prepared.append((entry["tenant"], entry["metric"], pairs, identity,
733	                             sid, clean))
734	        with self._lock:
735	            # Phase 2: replay the batch in input order against a private copy
736	            # of the touched series, so later entries see earlier ones.
737	            originals, merged = {}, {}
738	            new_stamps, overwritten = {}, {}
739	            results = []
740	            total_written = total_duplicates = 0
741	            for tenant, metric, pairs, identity, sid, clean in prepared:
742	                if sid not in merged:
743	                    originals[sid] = dict(self._samples.get(sid, ()))
744	                    merged[sid] = dict(originals[sid])
745	                    new_stamps[sid] = set()
746	                    overwritten[sid] = False
747	                state, stored = merged[sid], originals[sid]
748	                written = duplicates = 0
749	                for stamp, value in clean:
750	                    if stamp in state:
751	                        if state[stamp] != value:
752	                            if not overwrite:
753	                                raise ObsError(
754	                                    "conflict for %s at timestamp %d: "
755	                                    "stored=%r incoming=%r"
756	                                    % (sid, stamp, state[stamp], value))
757	                            if stamp in stored:
758	                                overwritten[sid] = True
759	                        else:
760	                            duplicates += 1
761	                            continue
762	                    else:
763	                        new_stamps[sid].add(stamp)
764	                    state[stamp] = value
765	                    written += 1
766	                results.append({"series_id": sid, "written": written,
767	                                "duplicates": duplicates})
768	                total_written += written
769	                total_duplicates += duplicates
770	            # Phase 3: per-tenant quota check on the batch's net increase.
771	            tenants = {}
772	            for tenant, metric, pairs, identity, sid, clean in prepared:
773	                usage = tenants.setdefault(tenant, {"sids": set(), "points": 0})
774	                if sid not in usage["sids"]:
775	                    usage["sids"].add(sid)
776	                    usage["points"] += len(new_stamps[sid])
777	            for tenant, usage in tenants.items():
778	                quota = self._quotas.get(tenant)
779	                if quota is None:
780	                    continue
781	                used_series = used_points = 0
782	                for sid_, row in self._series.items():
783	                    if row["tenant"] == tenant:
784	                        used_series += 1
785	                        used_points += len(self._samples[sid_])
786	                new_series = sum(1 for sid in usage["sids"] if sid not in self._series)
787	                new_points = usage["points"]
788	                limit_series = quota["max_series"]
789	                limit_points = quota["max_points"]
790	                if new_series and limit_series is not None \
791	                        and used_series + new_series > limit_series:
792	                    raise ObsError(
793	                        "quota exceeded for tenant %r: series %d+%d > max_series %s"
794	                        % (tenant, used_series, new_series, limit_series))
795	                if new_points and limit_points is not None \
796	                        and used_points + new_points > limit_points:
797	                    raise ObsError(
798	                        "quota exceeded for tenant %r: points %d+%d > max_points %s"
799	                        % (tenant, used_points, new_points, limit_points))
800	            # Phase 4: commit. Everything before this point was in-memory
801	            # simulation, so a rejection above leaves no trace anywhere.
802	            revision = None
803	            if commit and total_written:
804	                committed = set()
805	                for tenant, metric, pairs, identity, sid, clean in prepared:
806	                    if sid in committed:
807	                        continue
808	                    committed.add(sid)
809	                    if sid not in self._series:
810	                        self._series[sid] = {"series_id": sid, "tenant": tenant,
811	                                             "metric": metric, "labels": pairs,
812	                                             "identity": identity}
813	                        self._samples[sid] = []
814	                    if not new_stamps[sid] and not overwritten[sid]:
815	                        continue
816	                    self._samples[sid] = sorted(merged[sid].items())
817	                    if overwritten[sid]:
818	                        # A stored value was replaced: rewrite the file so a
819	                        # timestamp never occupies more than one physical line.
820	                        self._rewrite_points(sid)
821	                    else:
822	                        fresh = sorted((stamp, merged[sid][stamp])
823	                                       for stamp in new_stamps[sid])
824	                        with open(self._points_path(sid), "a",
825	                                  encoding="utf-8") as handle:
826	                            handle.write("".join(_line(ts, value)
827	                                                 for ts, value in fresh))
828	                            handle.flush()
829	                            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
830	                self._writes += 1
831	                revision = self._bump_revision()
832	                self._save_registry()
833	        result = {"written": total_written, "duplicates": total_duplicates,
834	                  "results": results}
835	        if return_revision:
836	            result["revision"] = revision if revision is not None \
837	                else self._revision_now()
838	        return result

840	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ export
841	    def export_snapshot(self, tenant, metric, labels=None, start_ms=None,
842	                        end_ms=None, matchers=None, read_token=None):
843	        """A verifiable snapshot of the matching series' raw samples.
844	
845	        Filters exactly like :meth:`query` (exact ``labels``, ``matchers`` and
846	        the closed ``[start_ms, end_ms]`` interval) and returns
847	        ``{"version": 1, "snapshot_id": ..., "entries": [...]}``. Each entry
848	        holds only ``tenant``, ``metric``, ``labels`` and ``samples`` (the
849	        in-range samples, ascending by timestamp); entries are ordered by
850	        ``series_id`` and registered series with no sample in range are
851	        omitted. ``snapshot_id`` is the SHA-256 of the sorted, compact JSON
852	        UTF-8 bytes of ``{"version": 1, "entries": [...]}``, so any instance
853	        can verify a snapshot before replaying it.
854	
855	        The whole export reads one coherent snapshot under a single lock
856	        acquisition and never changes series, samples, write counters, quotas,
857	        alerts, the revision or query results: exporting the same state twice
858	        yields byte-identical content. With ``read_token`` given the token is
859	        validated first (see :meth:`check_read_token`) and the export runs
860	        only once this instance has reached the token's revision.
861	        """
862	        if read_token is not None:
863	            self.check_read_token(read_token, tenant)
864	        compiled_matchers = compile_matchers(matchers)
865	        lo = None if start_ms is None else int(start_ms)
866	        hi = None if end_ms is None else int(end_ms)
867	        if lo is not None and hi is not None and hi < lo:
868	            raise ObsError("end_ms must be >= start_ms")
869	        entries = []
870	        for sid, series_labels, samples in self._matching_series(
871	                tenant, metric, labels, compiled_matchers):
872	            rows = [[stamp, value] for stamp, value in samples
873	                    if (lo is None or stamp >= lo) and (hi is None or stamp <= hi)]
874	            if not rows:
875	                continue
876	            entries.append({"tenant": tenant, "metric": metric,
877	                            "labels": series_labels, "samples": rows})
878	        digest = hashlib.sha256(_snapshot_bytes(
879	            {"version": 1, "entries": entries})).hexdigest()
880	        return {"version": 1, "snapshot_id": digest, "entries": entries}
881	
882	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ replay
883	    def replay_snapshot(self, snapshot, now_ms=None, overwrite=False,
884	                        dry_run=False, return_revision=False):
885	        """Validate and apply a snapshot produced by :meth:`export_snapshot`.
886	
887	        The snapshot is verified before anything is stored: ``version`` must
888	        be 1, ``snapshot_id`` must equal the SHA-256 digest of the canonical
889	        ``{"version": 1, "entries": [...]}`` document, and every entry is then
890	        checked by the :meth:`write_batch` rules (labels, samples, future
891	        timestamps against ``now_ms`` when given, conflicts, per-tenant
892	        quotas) — invalid input or a digest mismatch raises ``ObsError``
893	        (``400`` semantics), a conflict or quota breach raises ``ObsError``
894	        (``409`` semantics), and any failure leaves no in-memory or on-disk
895	        change behind.
896	
897	        With ``dry_run=True`` all validation and counting runs but nothing is
898	        applied and the result carries ``applied=False``; otherwise the batch
899	        commits and ``applied`` is ``True``. The result is ``{"written",
900	        "duplicates", "results", "applied"}`` with ``results`` in entry order.
901	        Replaying a snapshot onto the state it was exported from is a pure
902	        duplicate replay (``written == 0``, the write counter and the revision
903	        do not move); replaying onto a partial state fills in only the missing
904	        points. An empty ``entries`` list is a valid no-op snapshot. A real
905	        replay that stores anything increases the persistent revision by one.
906	        With ``return_revision=True`` (a boolean; anything else is rejected
907	        before any validation) the result also carries ``revision``: the
908	        commit revision, or the current revision when nothing was committed.
909	        """
910	        if not isinstance(dry_run, bool):
911	            raise ObsError("dry_run must be a boolean")
912	        self._clean_return_revision(return_revision)
913	        if now_ms is not None and (isinstance(now_ms, bool)
914	                                   or not isinstance(now_ms, int)):
915	            raise ObsError("now_ms must be a non-boolean integer timestamp in ms or None")
916	        if not isinstance(overwrite, bool):
917	            raise ObsError("overwrite must be a boolean")
918	        if not isinstance(snapshot, dict):
919	            raise ObsError("snapshot must be an object with version, "
920	                           "snapshot_id and entries")
921	        version = snapshot.get("version")
922	        if isinstance(version, bool) or version != 1:
923	            raise ObsError("unsupported snapshot version: %r" % (version,))
924	        entries = snapshot.get("entries")
925	        if not isinstance(entries, list):
926	            raise ObsError("snapshot entries must be a list")
927	        snapshot_id = snapshot.get("snapshot_id")
928	        if not isinstance(snapshot_id, str) or not snapshot_id:
929	            raise ObsError("snapshot_id must be a non-empty string")
930	        digest = hashlib.sha256(_snapshot_bytes(
931	            {"version": 1, "entries": entries})).hexdigest()
932	        if snapshot_id != digest:
933	            raise ObsError("snapshot_id does not match the entries digest")
934	        if not entries:
935	            result = {"written": 0, "duplicates": 0, "results": [],
936	                      "applied": not dry_run}
937	            if return_revision:
938	                result["revision"] = self._revision_now()
939	            return result
940	        result = self._apply_batch(entries, now=now_ms, overwrite=overwrite,
941	                                   commit=not dry_run,
942	                                   return_revision=return_revision)
943	        out = {"written": result["written"], "duplicates": result["duplicates"],
944	               "results": result["results"], "applied": not dry_run}
945	        if return_revision:
946	            out["revision"] = result["revision"]
947	        return out

950	    def _matching_series(self, tenant, metric, labels, compiled_matchers=()):
951	        """Snapshot of every matching series: sid, labels and raw samples.
952	
953	        Copied under one lock acquisition so a query can never mix samples from
954	        before and after a concurrent write or retention sweep. Exact ``labels``
955	        and the compiled ``matchers`` both filter the same raw series labels
956	        before any aggregation or grouping takes place.
957	        """
958	        with self._lock:
959	            ids = sorted(sid for sid, row in self._series.items()
960	                         if row["tenant"] == tenant and row["metric"] == metric
961	                         and matches_labels(dict(row["labels"]), labels)
962	                         and matchers_hold(dict(row["labels"]), compiled_matchers))
963	            return [(sid, dict(self._series[sid]["labels"]), list(self._samples[sid]))
964	                    for sid in ids]
965	
966	    def _samples_for(self, tenant, metric, labels, compiled_matchers=()):
967	        return [(sid, samples) for sid, _, samples in
968	                self._matching_series(tenant, metric, labels, compiled_matchers)]

970	    def _scan(self, tenant, metric, labels, start_ms, end_ms):
971	        """Raw samples of matching series inside ``[start, end]`` (internal).
972	
973	        Used where exact event counts matter (SLO numerator/denominator) and by
974	        rule evaluation to find candidate series.
975	        """
976	        lo = None if start_ms is None else int(start_ms)
977	        hi = None if end_ms is None else int(end_ms)
978	        out = []

995	        ``ObsError`` (``409`` semantics). The query itself never changes the

1002	        with each other and with ``labels`` by logical AND, apply to the raw

1004	        ``group_by`` included), and are validated up front even when no series

1086	    def _window_params(start_ms, end_ms, step_ms, window_ms, agg):
1087	        """Validate sliding-window arguments; return ``(start, end, step, window)``."""
1088	        if not isinstance(window_ms, int) or isinstance(window_ms, bool) or window_ms <= 0:

1091	            raise ObsError("sliding-window query requires an integer start_ms")
1092	        if not isinstance(end_ms, int) or isinstance(end_ms, bool):
1093	            raise ObsError("sliding-window query requires an integer end_ms")
1094	        if not isinstance(step_ms, int) or isinstance(step_ms, bool) or step_ms <= 0:
1095	            raise ObsError("sliding-window query requires a positive integer step_ms")
1096	        if end_ms < start_ms:
1097	            raise ObsError("end_ms must be >= start_ms")
1098	        if agg is None:
1099	            raise ObsError("sliding-window query requires agg")

1102	    def _window_grid(self, start_ms, end_ms, step_ms):
1103	        """The ``start_ms + k*step_ms`` evaluation times not past ``end_ms``."""
1104	        return range(start_ms, end_ms + 1, step_ms)

1106	    def _window_values(self, rows, window, times, agg):
1107	        """Aggregate the samples of ``(t - window, t]`` for each ``t``.
1108	
1109	        ``rows`` is a timestamp-sorted sample list shared by every time. A
1110	        sample at the evaluation time is included; one exactly one window
1111	        length earlier is excluded. Empty windows (no samples, regardless of
1112	        the aggregation, even ``count``) become ``None``.
1113	        """
1114	        points = []
1115	        index = 0
1116	        for t in times:
1117	            left = t - window
1118	            while index < len(rows) and rows[index][0] <= left:
1119	                index += 1
1120	            values = []
1121	            for cursor in range(index, len(rows)):
1122	                stamp = rows[cursor][0]
1123	                if stamp > t:
1124	                    break
1125	                values.append(rows[cursor][1])
1126	            points.append([t, None if not values else _aggregate(values, agg)])
1127	        return points

1129	    @staticmethod
1130	    def _counter_value(windowed, agg):
1131	        """``increase``/``rate`` of one series over one window's samples.
1132	
1133	        ``windowed`` is the timestamp-sorted samples of a single series inside
1134	        ``(t - window, t]``. Every sample actually in the window must be a
1135	        non-negative finite number, else the whole query fails. Fewer than two
1136	        samples (hence fewer than two distinct timestamps) yield ``None``.
1137	        """
1138	        for stamp, value in windowed:
1139	            if not math.isfinite(value) or value < 0:
1140	                raise ObsError(
1141	                    "aggregation %r requires non-negative finite samples, "
1142	                    "got %r at timestamp %d" % (agg, value, stamp))
1143	        if len(windowed) < 2:
1144	            return None
1145	        total = 0.0
1146	        previous = windowed[0][1]
1147	        for _, value in windowed[1:]:
1148	            # A drop means the counter reset: count only the later reading.
1149	            total += value - previous if value >= previous else value
1150	            previous = value
1151	        if agg == "increase":
1152	            return total
1153	        span_seconds = (windowed[-1][0] - windowed[0][0]) / 1000.0
1154	        return total / span_seconds

1156	    def _window_counter_points(self, rows, window, times, agg):
1157	        """Per-time ``increase``/``rate`` for one series over the time grid."""
1158	        points = []
1159	        index = 0
1160	        for t in times:
1161	            left = t - window
1162	            while index < len(rows) and rows[index][0] <= left:
1163	                index += 1
1164	            windowed = []
1165	            for cursor in range(index, len(rows)):
1166	                stamp = rows[cursor][0]
1167	                if stamp > t:
1168	                    break
1169	                windowed.append(rows[cursor])
1170	            points.append([t, self._counter_value(windowed, agg)])
1171	        return points

1173	    def _query_windows(self, tenant, metric, labels, lo, hi, step_ms, agg,
1174	                       group_by, window, compiled_matchers=()):
1175	        if group_by is not None:
1176	            if not isinstance(group_by, (list, tuple)):
1177	                raise ObsError("group_by must be a list of label keys")
1178	            keys = list(group_by)
1179	            for key in keys:
1180	                if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
1181	                    raise ObsError("group_by entries must be non-empty strings")
1182	            if len(set(keys)) != len(keys):
1183	                raise ObsError("group_by entries must not contain duplicates")
1184	        times = list(self._window_grid(lo, hi, step_ms))
1185	        matched = self._matching_series(tenant, metric, labels, compiled_matchers)
1186	        counter = agg in COUNTER_AGGREGATES
1187	        if group_by is None:
1188	            out = []
1189	            for sid, series_labels, samples in matched:
1190	                if counter:
1191	                    points = self._window_counter_points(samples, window, times, agg)
1192	                else:
1193	                    points = self._window_values(samples, window, times, agg)
1194	                out.append({"series_id": sid, "labels": dict(series_labels),
1195	                            "points": points})
1196	            return out
1197	        groups = {}
1198	        for sid, series_labels, samples in matched:
1199	            group_labels = {key: series_labels[key] for key in keys
1200	                            if key in series_labels}
1201	            token = tuple(sorted(group_labels.items()))
1202	            entry = groups.setdefault(token, {"labels": group_labels, "rows": []})
1203	            # The first window reads history before start_ms; no window reads
1204	            # anything past its own evaluation time, so no upper filter applies.
1205	            if counter:
1206	                # Counter aggregates are computed per series, never across
1207	                # series; the group sums the per-series results afterwards.
1208	                entry["rows"].append(
1209	                    self._window_counter_points(samples, window, times, agg))
1210	            else:
1211	                entry["rows"].extend(samples)
1212	        out = []
1213	        for token in sorted(groups):
1214	            entry = groups[token]
1215	            if counter:
1216	                points = []
1217	                for position, t in enumerate(times):
1218	                    values = [column[position][1] for column in entry["rows"]
1219	                              if column[position][1] is not None]
1220	                    points.append([t, sum(values) if values else None])
1221	            else:
1222	                rows = sorted(entry["rows"])
1223	                points = self._window_values(rows, window, times, agg)
1224	            out.append({"labels": entry["labels"], "points": points})
1225	        return out

1227	    def _bucket(self, rows, step_ms, agg, lo, hi):
1228	        """``None`` = nothing to report, ``[]`` = known empty, else the points."""
1229	        if step_ms is None:
1230	            if agg is None:
1231	                return [[stamp, value] for stamp, value in rows]
1232	            return None if not rows else [[rows[0][0], _aggregate([v for _, v in rows], agg)]]
1233	        step = int(step_ms)
1234	        groups = {}
1235	        for stamp, value in rows:
1236	            groups.setdefault(stamp - (stamp % step), []).append(value)
1237	        if not groups:
1238	            return None
1239	        keys = sorted(groups)
1240	        start = max(keys[0], lo - (lo % step)) if lo is not None else keys[0]
1241	        end = min(keys[-1], hi - (hi % step)) if hi is not None else keys[-1]
1242	        return [[key, _aggregate(groups[key], agg) if key in groups else None]
1243	                for key in range(start, end + 1, step)]

1245	    def _query_grouped(self, tenant, metric, labels, lo, hi, step_ms, agg, group_by,
1246	                       compiled_matchers=()):
1247	        """Cross-series aggregation: one row per distinct ``group_by`` tuple.
1248	
1249	        The raw in-range samples of every series in a group are pooled before
1250	        aggregating (no per-series pre-averaging), so samples from different
1251	        series at the same timestamp each count. A group key absent from a
1252	        series simply does not appear in that group's labels; a missing key
1253	        and an empty-string value therefore land in different groups.
1254	        """
1255	        if not isinstance(group_by, (list, tuple)):
1256	            raise ObsError("group_by must be a list of label keys")
1257	        keys = list(group_by)
1258	        for key in keys:
1259	            if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
1260	                raise ObsError("group_by entries must be non-empty strings")
1261	        if len(set(keys)) != len(keys):
1262	            raise ObsError("group_by entries must not contain duplicates")
1263	        if agg is None:
1264	            raise ObsError("group_by requires agg")
1265	        groups = {}
1266	        for sid, samples in self._samples_for(tenant, metric, labels,
1267	                                              compiled_matchers):
1268	            series_labels = dict(self._series[sid]["labels"])
1269	            group_labels = {key: series_labels[key] for key in keys
1270	                            if key in series_labels}
1271	            token = tuple(sorted(group_labels.items()))
1272	            entry = groups.setdefault(token, {"labels": group_labels, "rows": []})
1273	            entry["rows"].extend(item for item in samples
1274	                                 if (lo is None or item[0] >= lo)
1275	                                 and (hi is None or item[0] <= hi))
1276	        out = []
1277	        for token in sorted(groups):
1278	            entry = groups[token]
1279	            rows = sorted(entry["rows"])
1280	            if step_ms is None:
1281	                points = [] if not rows else \
1282	                    [[rows[0][0], _aggregate([value for _, value in rows], agg)]]
1283	            else:
1284	                points = self._bucket(rows, step_ms, agg, lo, hi) or []
1285	            out.append({"labels": entry["labels"], "points": points})
1286	        return out

1288	    def rollup(self, tenant, metric, labels, window_ms, agg):
1289	        """Downsampled series over the whole stored range, ordered by series_id."""
1290	        if agg not in AGGREGATES:
1291	            raise ObsError("unknown aggregation: %r" % (agg,))
1292	        if not _num(window_ms) or int(window_ms) <= 0:
1293	            raise ObsError("window_ms must be a positive number")

1295	                 "points": [point for point in item["points"] if point[1] is not None]}
1296	                for item in self.query(tenant, metric, labels=labels,
1297	                                       step_ms=int(window_ms), agg=agg)]

1387	    def run_retention(self, now_ms, tenant=None, dry_run=False,

1394	        is ``now_ms - retention_ms`` and only samples with
1395	        ``timestamp_ms < cutoff_ms`` are dropped (a sample exactly at the
1396	        cutoff is kept); a ``null`` policy cleans nothing and reports a
1397	        ``null`` cutoff with zero deletions. Affected point files are rewritten
1398	        in compacted form — one physical record per timestamp, the final value
1399	        winning — and empty series stay registered. The freed points count
1400	        against the tenant's quota immediately.

1404	        ``dry_run=True`` the same report is produced but memory, files, quotas,
1405	        the write counter and the revision are left untouched. A real run that
1406	        deletes at least one sample increases the persistent revision by one;
1407	        a run that deletes nothing does not. Returns
1408	        ``{"dry_run": bool, "tenants": [...]}`` with one
1409	        ``{"tenant", "cutoff_ms", "dropped", "affected_series",
1410	        "remaining_points", "compacted_series"}`` entry per processed tenant,
1411	        in lexicographic tenant order. With ``return_revision=True`` (a
1412	        boolean; anything else is rejected before any validation) the result
1413	        also carries ``revision``: the commit revision, or the current
1414	        revision when nothing was committed.

1416	        if isinstance(now_ms, bool) or not isinstance(now_ms, int):
1417	            raise ObsError("now_ms must be a non-boolean integer timestamp in ms")
1418	        if tenant is not None:
1419	            tenant = self._clean_tenant(tenant)
1420	        if not isinstance(dry_run, bool):
1421	            raise ObsError("dry_run must be a boolean")
1422	        self._clean_return_revision(return_revision)
1423	        revision = None
1424	        with self._lock:
1425	            names = [tenant] if tenant is not None else sorted(self._retention)
1426	            results = []
1427	            dropped_total = 0
1428	            for name in names:
1429	                policy = self._retention.get(name)
1430	                sids = sorted(sid for sid, row in self._series.items()
1431	                              if row["tenant"] == name)
1432	                if policy is None:
1433	                    results.append({
1434	                        "tenant": name, "cutoff_ms": None, "dropped": 0,
1435	                        "affected_series": 0,
1436	                        "remaining_points":
1437	                            sum(len(self._samples[sid]) for sid in sids),
1438	                        "compacted_series": 0})

1440	                cutoff = now_ms - policy

1444	                            if item[0] >= cutoff]

1448	                        dropped += removed

            out.append([int(stamp), float(value)])
        except ValueError:
            raise ObsError("sample %r must look like timestamp_ms:value" % entry)

def _run(args, store, engine, access):
    if args.command == "serve":
        return run_server(store, engine, args.host, args.port, access=access)
    if args.command == "principal-create":
        _emit(access.create_principal(args.id, args.token, args.role, args.tenant))
    elif args.command == "principal-list":
        _emit({"principals": access.list_principals()})
    elif args.command == "principal-revoke":
        _emit(access.revoke_principal(args.id))
    elif args.command == "quota-set":
        _emit(store.set_quota(args.tenant, args.max_series, args.max_points))
    elif args.command == "quota-get":
        _emit(store.get_quota(args.tenant))
    elif args.command == "retention-set":
        _emit(store.set_retention(args.tenant, args.retention_ms))
    elif args.command == "retention-get":
        _emit(store.get_retention(args.tenant))
    elif args.command == "retention-run":
        _emit(store.run_retention(args.now_ms, tenant=args.tenant,
                                  dry_run=args.dry_run,
                                  return_revision=args.return_revision))
    elif args.command == "consistency-token":
        _emit(store.consistency_token(args.tenant))
    elif args.command == "write":
        _emit(store.write(args.tenant, args.metric, _labels(args.label),
                          _samples(args.sample), now=args.now_ms,
                          overwrite=args.overwrite,
                          return_revision=args.return_revision))
    elif args.command == "write-batch":
        try:
            entries = json.loads(args.entries)
        except ValueError:
            raise ObsError("--entries must be a JSON array of entry objects")
        _emit(store.write_batch(entries, now=args.now_ms, overwrite=args.overwrite,
                                return_revision=args.return_revision))
    elif args.command == "query":
        group_by = None
        if args.group_by is not None:
            try:
                group_by = json.loads(args.group_by)
            except ValueError:
                raise ObsError("--group-by must be a JSON array of label keys")
        matchers = parse_matchers_text(args.matchers, "--matchers")
        rows = store.query(args.tenant, args.metric, labels=_labels(args.label),
                           start_ms=args.start, end_ms=args.end, step_ms=args.step,
                           agg=args.agg, group_by=group_by, window_ms=args.window_ms,
                           matchers=matchers, read_token=args.read_token)
        _emit({"series": [{"labels": row["labels"], "points": row["points"]} for row in rows]})
    elif args.command == "export":
        matchers = parse_matchers_text(args.matchers, "--matchers")
        _emit(store.export_snapshot(args.tenant, args.metric,
                                    labels=_labels(args.label),
                                    start_ms=args.start, end_ms=args.end,
                                    matchers=matchers, read_token=args.read_token))
    elif args.command == "replay":
        try:
            snapshot = json.loads(args.snapshot)
        except ValueError:
            raise ObsError("--snapshot must be a JSON object as produced by export")
        _emit(store.replay_snapshot(snapshot, now_ms=args.now_ms,
                                    overwrite=args.overwrite,
                                    dry_run=args.dry_run,
                                    return_revision=args.return_revision))
    elif args.command == "rule-add":
        _emit(engine.add_rule({
            "id": args.id, "tenant": args.tenant, "metric": args.metric,
            "labels": _labels(args.label), "comparator": args.comparator,
            "threshold": args.threshold, "for_ms": args.for_ms, "window_ms": args.window_ms,
            "agg": args.agg, "severity": args.severity,
            "annotations": _labels(args.annotation)}))
    elif args.command == "eval":
        _emit(engine.evaluate(args.now_ms))
    elif args.command == "route-add":
        _emit(engine.add_route({
            "id": args.id, "tenant": args.tenant, "target": args.target,
            "labels": _labels(args.label), "severities": args.severity,
            "events": args.event, "repeat_ms": args.repeat_ms}))
    elif args.command == "route-list":
        _emit({"routes": engine.list_routes(args.tenant)})
    elif args.command == "notification-list":
        _emit({"notifications": engine.list_notifications(
            tenant=args.tenant, route_id=args.route_id, alert_id=args.alert_id,
            acked=None if args.acked is None else args.acked == "true")})
    elif args.command == "notification-ack":
        _emit(engine.ack_notification(args.id))
    elif args.command == "alerts":
        _emit({"alerts": engine.list_alerts(args.tenant, args.state)})
    elif args.command == "silence-add":
        _emit(engine.add_silence(args.tenant, _labels(args.label), args.starts_ms,
                                 args.ends_ms, args.reason))
    elif args.command == "slo" and args.slo_command == "set":
        _emit(engine.set_slo(args.tenant, args.name, args.metric, _labels(args.label),
                             args.good_comparator, args.threshold, args.target_ratio,
                             args.window_ms))
    elif args.command == "slo":
        _emit(engine.slo_status(args.name, args.now_ms, tenant=args.tenant,
                                read_token=args.read_token))
    else:
        return _fail("unknown command: %s" % args.command)
    return 0
def main(argv=None):
    """Dispatch one CLI invocation; 0 on success, non-zero + JSON error otherwise."""
    parser = _build_parser()
    try:
        args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    except SystemExit as exc:
        return _fail("invalid arguments (exit %s)" % exc.code)
    try:
        data_dir = os.path.abspath(args.data_dir)
        store = SeriesStore(data_dir)
        return _run(args, store, AlertEngine(store, data_dir), AccessControl(data_dir))
    except ObsError as exc:
        return _fail(exc)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
        return _fail("%s: %s" % (type(exc).__name__, exc))
if __name__ == "__main__":  # pragma: no cover
    sys.exit(main())
