1	# obsd
2	
3	Minimal, dependency-free backend skeleton for **metrics ingestion, alerting and
4	SLO tracking**. Python 3.10+, standard library only, offline, deterministic
5	(every time-dependent entry point takes an injected `now_ms`).
6	
7	The lane goal is a metrics collection, alerting and SLO backend that grows
8	towards time-series writes and downsampling, label indexing and a query subset,
9	aggregation and sliding windows, alert rules with silencing and inhibition,
10	notification routing and dedup, SLO and error-budget math, retention and
11	compaction, multi-tenant quota, access control and audit, and consistent reads
12	under high availability. This seed implements the first, smallest *real* slice of
13	each of those areas.
14	
15	## Run
16	
17	```bash
18	# HTTP API (data dir flag is global and comes BEFORE the subcommand)
19	python3 -m obsd --data-dir ./obsd_data serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080
20	
21	# test suite
22	python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
23	```
24	
25	Both commands are run offline with the system interpreter; no third-party
26	package is imported anywhere.
27	
28	## CLI
29	
30	`python3 -m obsd [--data-dir ./obsd_data] <command> ...` prints exactly one line
31	of JSON on stdout. On error it prints one line of JSON (`{"error":"..."}`) on
32	stderr and exits non-zero.
33	
34	| Command | Example |
35	| --- | --- |
36	| `serve` | `python3 -m obsd --data-dir ./obsd_data serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080` |
37	| `quota-set` | `python3 -m obsd quota-set --tenant acme --max-series 1000 --max-points 1000000` |
38	| `quota-get` | `python3 -m obsd quota-get --tenant acme` |
39	| `retention-set` | `python3 -m obsd retention-set --tenant acme --retention-ms 86400000` (omit `--retention-ms` for no cleanup) |
40	| `retention-get` | `python3 -m obsd retention-get --tenant acme` |
41	| `retention-run` | `python3 -m obsd retention-run --now-ms 2000 [--tenant acme] [--dry-run] [--return-revision]` |
42	| `consistency-token` | `python3 -m obsd consistency-token --tenant acme` |
43	| `write` | `python3 -m obsd write --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --label host=a --sample 1000:12.5 --now-ms 2000 [--return-revision]` |
44	| `write-batch` | `python3 -m obsd write-batch --entries '[{"tenant":"acme","metric":"latency_ms","samples":[[1000,12.5]]}]' --now-ms 2000 [--return-revision]` |
45	| `query` | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --start 0 --end 5000 --step 1000 --agg avg [--read-token T]` |
46	| `query` (grouped) | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --agg avg --group-by '["host"]'` |
47	| `query` (matchers) | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --matchers '[{"key":"host","op":"=~","value":"api-.*"}]'` |
48	| `query` (sliding window) | `python3 -m obsd query --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --start 0 --end 5000 --step 1000 --window-ms 5000 --agg avg` |
49	| `export` | `python3 -m obsd export --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --start 0 --end 5000 [--read-token T]` |
50	| `replay` | `python3 -m obsd replay --snapshot '{"version":1,"snapshot_id":"...","entries":[...]}' --now-ms 5000 [--return-revision]` |
51	| `rule-add` | `python3 -m obsd rule-add --tenant acme --metric latency_ms --comparator "<" --threshold 10 --window-ms 60000 --for-ms 30000 --agg avg --severity warning` |
52	| `eval` | `python3 -m obsd eval --now-ms 68000` |
53	| `alerts` | `python3 -m obsd alerts --tenant acme --state firing` |
54	| `silence-add` | `python3 -m obsd silence-add --tenant acme --starts-ms 0 --ends-ms 90000 --reason maintenance` |
55	| `route-add` | `python3 -m obsd route-add --tenant acme --target pager --label host=a --severity critical --event firing --repeat-ms 300000` |
56	| `route-list` | `python3 -m obsd route-list --tenant acme` |
57	| `notification-list` | `python3 -m obsd notification-list --tenant acme --acked false` |
58	| `notification-ack` | `python3 -m obsd notification-ack --id notification-00001` |
59	| `slo set` | `python3 -m obsd slo set --tenant acme --name availability --metric latency_ms --good-comparator ">=" --threshold 1 --target-ratio 0.9 --window-ms 60000` |
60	| `slo status` | `python3 -m obsd slo status --name availability --now-ms 60000 [--read-token T]` |
61	| `principal-create` | `python3 -m obsd principal-create --id ops --token s3cret --role admin --tenant acme --tenant globex` |
62	| `principal-list` | `python3 -m obsd principal-list` |
63	| `principal-revoke` | `python3 -m obsd principal-revoke --id ops` |
64	
65	## HTTP API
66	
67	Errors are always JSON: `{"error":"..."}` with status 400 (bad request,
68	including `invalid read token`), 404 (unknown resource) or 409 (write
69	conflict, quota exceeded or `read revision unavailable`).
70	
71	| Method | Path | Request | Response |
72	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
73	| GET | `/healthz` | – | `200 {"ok":true}` |
74	| GET | `/v1/consistency-token` | `?tenant=` | `200 {"tenant","token","revision"}` — mints a read-consistency token for the tenant |
75	| POST | `/v1/series` | `{"tenant","metric","labels","samples":[[ts,value],...],"now_ms"?,"overwrite"?,"return_revision"?}` | `202 {"written":n,"duplicates":m,"series_id":"..."}` (plus `"revision"` when `return_revision` is true), `400` on malformed input or a non-boolean `now_ms`/`overwrite`/`return_revision` (an explicit `null` `overwrite`/`return_revision` is rejected, not treated as `false`), `409` on conflicting timestamp or quota exceeded |
76	| POST | `/v1/series/batch` | `{"entries":[{"tenant","metric","samples","labels"?},...],"now_ms"?,"overwrite"?,"return_revision"?}` | `202 {"written":n,"duplicates":m,"results":[{"series_id","written","duplicates"},...]}` (plus `"revision"` when `return_revision` is true), `400` on malformed entries, `409` on conflict or quota exceeded |
77	| GET | `/v1/query` | `?tenant=&metric=&label.k=v&start=&end=&step=&agg=&group_by=&window=&matchers=&read_token=` (group_by and matchers are JSON arrays; matchers holds `{"key","op","value"}` objects) | `200 {"series":[{"labels":{...},"points":[[ts,value\|null],...]}]}`, `400` on an invalid read token, `409` while the token's revision is unavailable |
78	| GET | `/v1/export` | `?tenant=&metric=&label.k=v&start=&end=&matchers=&read_token=` (same filters and closed-interval semantics as `/v1/query`) | `200 {"version":1,"snapshot_id":"...","entries":[{"tenant","metric","labels","samples"},...]}`, `400`/`409` on read-token failures |
79	| POST | `/v1/replay` | `{"version":1,"snapshot_id":"...","entries":[...],"now_ms"?,"overwrite"?,"dry_run"?,"return_revision"?}` | `202 {"written":n,"duplicates":m,"results":[...],"applied":true}` (`200` with `"applied":false` for a dry run; plus `"revision"` when `return_revision` is true), `400` on invalid input or digest mismatch, `409` on conflict or quota exceeded |
80	| POST | `/v1/quotas` | `{"tenant","max_series":n\|null,"max_points":n\|null}` | `200 {"tenant","max_series","max_points","series","points"}`; invalid tenant/limits give `400` and leave config untouched |
81	| GET | `/v1/quotas` | `?tenant=` | `200 {"tenant","max_series","max_points","series","points"}` (unconfigured tenant reports `null` limits and real usage) |
82	| POST | `/v1/retention/policies` | `{"tenant","retention_ms":n\|null}` | `200 {"tenant","retention_ms","series","points"}`; invalid tenant/policy or unknown fields give `400` and leave config untouched |
83	| GET | `/v1/retention/policies` | `?tenant=` | `200 {"tenant","retention_ms","series","points"}` (unconfigured tenant reports a `null` policy and real usage) |
84	| POST | `/v1/retention/run` | `{"now_ms":n,"tenant"?,"dry_run"?,"return_revision"?}` | `200 {"dry_run":b,"tenants":[{"tenant","cutoff_ms","dropped","affected_series","remaining_points","compacted_series"},...]}` (plus `"revision"` when `return_revision` is true); missing/non-integer `now_ms`, non-boolean `dry_run`/`return_revision` or unknown fields give `400` |
85	| POST | `/v1/rules` | rule object | `201` stored rule |
86	| GET | `/v1/rules` | `?tenant=` | `200 {"rules":[...]}` |
87	| POST | `/v1/evaluate` | `{"now_ms":n}` | `200 {"firing":[...],"silenced":[...],"inhibited":[...],"resolved":[...]}` |
88	| GET | `/v1/alerts` | `?tenant=&state=` | `200 {"alerts":[...]}` |
89	| POST | `/v1/silences` | `{"tenant","labels","starts_ms","ends_ms","reason"}` | `201` stored silence |
90	| POST | `/v1/inhibitions` | `{"source_severity","target_severity","same_labels"?}` | `201` stored inhibition; `same_labels` must be a real boolean (omitted defaults to `true`; `null`, numbers and strings are rejected with `400` and change nothing) |
91	| POST | `/v1/notification-routes` | `{"tenant","target","labels"?,"severities"?,"events"?,"repeat_ms"?,"id"?}` | `201` stored route; `400` invalid, `409` duplicate id |
92	| GET | `/v1/notification-routes` | `?tenant=` | `200 {"routes":[...]}` |
93	| DELETE | `/v1/notification-routes/{id}` | – | `200 {"deleted":id}`; `404` unknown route (notifications are kept) |
94	| GET | `/v1/notifications` | `?tenant=&route_id=&alert_id=&acked=` | `200 {"notifications":[...]}` (read-only, never consumes) |
95	| POST | `/v1/notifications/{id}/ack` | – | `200` stored notification (re-ack returns the same record); `404` unknown notification |
96	| POST | `/v1/slos` | `{"tenant","name","metric","labels","good_comparator","threshold","target_ratio","window_ms"}` | `201` stored SLO |
97	| GET | `/v1/slos/status` | `?tenant=&name=&now_ms=&read_token=` | `200` SLO status object, `400`/`409` on read-token failures |
98	| GET | `/v1/stats` | – | `200 {"store":{...},"alerts":n}` |
99	| GET | `/v1/audit` | `?tenant=&principal_id=&outcome=&after_seq=&limit=` | `200 {"entries":[{"seq","principal_id","method","path","tenant","outcome","status"},...]}` ascending by `seq` (admin only) |
100	
101	**Access control and audit.** Principals are managed locally through the CLI
102	(`principal-create`/`principal-list`/`principal-revoke`); a principal is a
103	unique `--id`, a non-empty `--token`, a `--role` of `viewer`, `writer` or
104	`admin`, and at least one `--tenant` scope. Only the token's SHA-256 digest is
105	persisted (`access.json`); the token itself never appears in any output,
106	listing or audit record. A duplicate id is a conflict (`409` semantics), an
107	unknown id on revoke is `unknown principal: ...` (`404` semantics). While no
108	`access.json` exists, access control is off: every request stays anonymous,
109	nothing returns `401`/`403`, no audit records are written and `/healthz` is
110	always public either way.
111	
112	Once the config exists, every non-`/healthz` request must carry
113	`Authorization: Bearer <token>`: a missing, malformed or unknown token gets
114	`401 {"error":"unauthorized"}`. An authenticated principal whose role or
115	tenant scope does not cover the request gets `403 {"error":"forbidden"}`.
116	`viewer` reads resources inside its tenant scope; `writer` additionally
117	writes series, manages rules, silences, routes and SLOs and acknowledges
118	notifications inside its scope; `admin` additionally runs quotas, inhibitions,
119	evaluation, stats and the audit endpoint, and is the only role allowed to run
120	cross-tenant operations (requests with no single tenant, such as an
121	unfiltered `GET /v1/alerts`). Batch writes are checked per entry: if any
122	entry's tenant is outside the caller's scope the whole batch is rejected with
123	`403` before anything is written, preserving atomicity. Principals created or
124	revoked through the CLI take effect on a running server without a restart.
125	
126	Every non-`/healthz` request — authentication rejections, authorization
127	denials and business failures included — appends one persistent audit record
128	to `audit.jsonl` with a monotonically increasing `seq`:
129	`{"seq","principal_id","method","path","tenant","outcome","status"}`, where
130	`principal_id` is `null` when the request could not be authenticated,
131	`tenant` is `null` when the request has no single tenant, and `outcome` is
132	`allowed` (authorized, status < 400), `denied` (`401`/`403`) or `failed`
133	(authorized but the business logic rejected it). The log is reloaded on
134	startup, so records and the `seq` sequence survive restarts.
135	`GET /v1/audit` (admin only) filters by `tenant`, `principal_id`, `outcome`
136	and `after_seq` (entries with `seq > after_seq`) and pages with a positive
137	integer `limit`; invalid filters are `400`, non-admin access is `403`.
138	
139	## Data model
140	
141	A series identity is `(tenant, metric, sorted(label pairs))`. The canonical
142	identity string joins the tenant, the metric and every `key=value` label pair
143	(sorted by key) with `\n`:
144	
145	```
146	acme\nlatency_ms\nhost=a\nregion=eu
147	```
148	
149	`series_id = sha256(canonical_identity).hexdigest()`, so the same logical series
150	always maps to the same 64-character id, independent of label insertion order.
151	
152	Storage layout (all writes atomic via temp file + `os.replace`):
153	
154	```
155	<data-dir>/series.json              registry: series_id -> tenant/metric/labels
156	<data-dir>/points/<series_id>.jsonl one {"t":ts,"v":value} object per line
157	<data-dir>/quotas.json              tenant -> {"max_series","max_points"} limits
158	<data-dir>/retention.json           tenant -> {"retention_ms"} retention policies
159	<data-dir>/rules.json               <data-dir>/alerts.json
160	<data-dir>/slos.json                <data-dir>/silences.json
161	<data-dir>/inhibitions.json         <data-dir>/counters.json
162	<data-dir>/routes.json              <data-dir>/notifications.json
163	<data-dir>/notify_state.json        per-(route, alert) notification dedup state
164	<data-dir>/access.json              principals: id, token SHA-256 digest, role, tenants
165	<data-dir>/audit.jsonl              one audit record per line, seq monotonically increasing
166	<data-dir>/revision.json            persistent revision counter + token-signing secret
167	```
168	
169	A directory written before quotas existed simply has no `quotas.json`, which
170	means every tenant is unlimited; limits and usage are reloaded together on
171	construction so a reopen always reports a consistent snapshot.
172	
173	`SeriesStore` and `AlertEngine` each guard their state with a
174	`threading.RLock`, so the threaded HTTP server can serve concurrent requests; all
175	state is reloaded from disk on construction, so a restart preserves series,
176	points, rules, alerts, silences, inhibitions, SLOs, notification routes and
177	queued notifications.
178	
179	## Semantics and formulas
180	
181	**Idempotent write.** `write(tenant, metric, labels, samples, now=None,
182	overwrite=False)` stores `(timestamp_ms, value)` pairs. Writing an existing
183	`(series, timestamp)` with the *same* value is a duplicate: it changes nothing
184	and is counted in `duplicates`. A *different* value for a stored timestamp is a
185	conflict: it raises `ObsError` (`409` over HTTP) unless `overwrite=True`, in
186	which case the stored value is replaced and counted in `written`. A timestamp
187	greater than the injected `now` (when `now` is given) is rejected. `now` is
188	`None`/omitted (no future check) or a non-boolean integer; `overwrite` must be
189	a boolean (default `False`). Anything else raises `ObsError` (`400` over HTTP)
190	before any validation or state change: no series, points, write counter, quota
191	usage or temp file is touched.
192	
193	**Atomic multi-series write.** `write_batch(entries, now=None, overwrite=False)`
194	(also `POST /v1/series/batch` and the CLI `write-batch --entries '<json>'`)
195	applies a non-empty list of `{"tenant","metric","samples","labels"?}` entries
196	(`labels` omitted means `{}`, no other keys allowed) as one all-or-nothing
197	unit. Entries may span tenants and metrics and may repeat a series. `now` is
198	`null`/omitted (no future check) or a non-boolean integer; `overwrite` must be
199	a boolean (default `false`). The whole batch is validated before any conflict
200	is reported, and all conflicts before any quota check. Entries and their
201	samples are then applied in input order, so a later entry sees the earlier
202	entries of the same batch: a same-value restatement is a duplicate, a
203	differing value conflicts unless `overwrite` (then it replaces and counts as
204	written). The result is `{"written","duplicates","results"}` with one
205	`{"series_id","written","duplicates"}` per entry in input order; the totals
206	are the per-entry sums. A successful batch with `written > 0` increases
207	`stats()["writes"]` by exactly one; a pure-duplicate batch increases nothing.
208	Quotas are charged per tenant with the batch's net new series and distinct new
209	timestamps — duplicates and overwrites add no occupancy, and only dimensions
210	that actually increase are checked. Any rejection (structure, missing fields,
211	per-entry validation, future samples → `400`; conflict or quota → `409`)
212	leaves no series, sample or write-count change behind, on disk included, and
213	concurrent queries and quota reads only ever see the state before or after the
214	whole batch. Replaying the same batch re-judges duplicates and overwrites in
215	the same order.
216	
217	**Snapshot export and replay.** `export_snapshot(tenant, metric, labels=None,
218	start_ms=None, end_ms=None, matchers=None)` (also `GET /v1/export` and the CLI
219	`export`) captures the raw samples of every matching series as a verifiable
220	document `{"version": 1, "snapshot_id": ..., "entries": [...]}`. The filters
221	and the closed `[start_ms, end_ms]` interval behave exactly as in `query`.
222	Each entry holds only `tenant`, `metric`, `labels` and `samples` (ascending by
223	timestamp); entries are ordered by `series_id` and registered series with no
224	sample in range are omitted. `snapshot_id` is the SHA-256 of the sorted,
225	compact JSON UTF-8 bytes of `{"version": 1, "entries": [...]}`. The export
226	reads one coherent snapshot under a single lock acquisition and never changes
227	write counters, quotas, alerts or query results, so exporting the same state
228	twice yields identical content.
229	
230	`replay_snapshot(snapshot, now_ms=None, overwrite=False, dry_run=False)` (also
231	`POST /v1/replay` and the CLI `replay --snapshot '<json>'`) verifies the
232	document before storing anything: the version must be 1, `snapshot_id` must
233	match the entries digest, and every entry then goes through the `write_batch`
234	rules (labels, samples, future timestamps against `now_ms` when given,
235	conflicts, per-tenant quotas). Invalid input or a digest mismatch is a `400`,
236	a conflict or quota breach a `409`, and any failure leaves no in-memory or
237	on-disk change behind. The result is `{"written", "duplicates", "results",
238	"applied"}` with `results` in entry order. A dry run (`dry_run=true` /
239	`--dry-run`) performs all validation and counting but applies nothing and
240	reports `applied: false`; a real replay reports `applied: true` (`202` over
241	HTTP, `200` for a dry run). Replaying a snapshot onto the state it came from
242	is a pure duplicate replay (`written == 0`, the write counter does not move),
243	replaying onto a partial state fills in only the missing points, and a replay
244	after a restart re-judges exactly as an in-process one. Replay never mints new
245	series identities and does not alter labels, tenant isolation, query
246	aggregation, alert or SLO semantics. With access control enabled, export is a
247	`read` operation scoped to the requested tenant and replay is a `write`
248	operation checked per entry — any entry outside the caller's scope rejects the
249	whole replay with `403` — and both are audited like every other endpoint.
250	
251	**Bucketing.** `query(..., step_ms=step, agg=agg)` assigns a sample with
252	timestamp `t` to bucket `b = t - (t % step)`, i.e. buckets are
253	left-closed/right-open (`[b, b+step)`) on epoch multiples. Every bucket from the
254	first non-empty bucket to the last non-empty bucket that also lies inside
255	`[start_ms, end_ms]` is emitted, and buckets with no sample are emitted as
256	`[b, null]`. Bucket value = `agg` over the samples in the bucket, where `agg` is
257	one of `sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count`. A series whose range contains no
258	sample is still listed with an empty `points` list. With `agg` and *no*
259	`step_ms` the whole `[start_ms, end_ms]` range is a single bucket. With neither,
260	raw samples are returned in `[timestamp, value]` order. `rollup(tenant, metric,
261	labels, window_ms, agg)` is `query` with `step_ms = window_ms` over the whole
262	stored range, with empty buckets dropped; output is ordered by `series_id`, so
263	it is deterministic.
264	
265	**Label matchers.** In addition to exact `labels` / `label.k=v` filtering,
266	`query` accepts `matchers` (`matchers` on `GET /v1/query`, `--matchers` on the
267	CLI): a JSON array of objects containing exactly `key` (non-empty string),
268	`op` and `value` (string, may be empty). Ops are `=` / `!=` (exact whole-string
269	equality and negation) and `=~` / `!~` (Python `re` syntax matched against the
270	*whole* label value via full match, case-sensitive and Unicode-aware, and its
271	negation). Omitting the parameter, passing Python `None`, or sending `[]` adds
272	no condition; an explicit JSON `null` or empty text is rejected (HTTP/CLI).
273	Matchers combine with each other and with the exact label filters by logical
274	AND — including several matchers on the same key — apply to raw series labels
275	before bucketing or grouping (labels absent from `group_by` count too), and are
276	restricted to the requested `tenant` and `metric`; `tenant`, `metric` and
277	`series_id` are not implicit labels. A missing key never satisfies `=`/`=~` but
278	always satisfies `!=`/`!~`, so `=~ ""` selects only series where the key exists
279	with an empty value (grouping still separates a missing key from an empty
280	value). `api-.*` matches `api-a` but not `xapi-a`. Duplicate matchers never
281	duplicate series, matcher order is irrelevant, and contradictory matchers
282	yield an empty result. Invalid JSON, a non-array, non-object elements, missing
283	or extra fields, wrong types, an empty `key`, an unsupported `op` or an invalid
284	regex raise `ObsError` (`400` over HTTP, one JSON error line on stderr for the
285	CLI); every matcher is validated even when no candidate series exists.
286	
287	**Grouped query.** `query(..., agg=agg, group_by=[keys...])` aggregates *across*
288	series: matching series (same tenant/metric/label filters and `[start_ms,
289	end_ms]` range as above) are bucketed into groups by the values of the given
290	label keys, and the raw in-range samples of all series in a group are pooled
291	before `agg` is applied — samples from different series at the same timestamp
292	count individually. `group_by=[]` merges every matching series into one group.
293	Each result row carries only `labels` (the group keys actually present on the
294	group's series — a missing key and an empty-string value form different
295	groups) and `points`; rows are ordered lexicographically by their sorted label
296	pairs. Bucketing follows the same rules as the per-series query (epoch-aligned
297	left-closed buckets with `null` gaps, or a single point at the group's
298	earliest sample without `step_ms`). A group whose series have no sample in
299	range is still listed with empty `points`; no matching series at all yields an
300	empty `series` array. `group_by` must be a list of distinct non-empty strings
301	and requires `agg`; violations raise `ObsError` (`400` over HTTP, one JSON
302	error line on stderr for the CLI).
303	
304	**Sliding-window query.** `query(..., start_ms=start, end_ms=end, step_ms=step,
305	agg=agg, window_ms=window)` switches to a separate mode the moment `window_ms`
306	is supplied (it is optional in every binding: `window` on `GET /v1/query`,
307	`--window-ms` on the CLI). In this mode `start_ms`, `end_ms`, `step_ms` and
308	`agg` are all required; `start_ms` and `end_ms` must be integer milliseconds,
309	`step_ms` and `window_ms` positive integer milliseconds, and `end_ms >=
310	start_ms` (bools, fractions and missing/unknown values are rejected). Evaluation
311	times are `t = start + k*step` for `k = 0, 1, ...`, keeping only times
312	`t <= end`; the output point timestamp is the evaluation time itself. The step
313	need not divide the window and windows are never aligned to fixed buckets.
314	
315	Each evaluation aggregates the raw samples in the half-open interval
316	`(t - window_ms, t]`: the left edge is excluded (a sample exactly one window
317	length earlier does not count), the right edge included (a sample at `t`
318	does). `start_ms` only constrains the output grid — the first window at
319	`start` also reads history older than `start`; no window ever reads a sample
320	newer than its own evaluation time. The aggregation uses the same meanings as
321	bucketing (`sum`, `avg`, `min`, `max`, `count`), and a window containing no
322	sample emits `[t, null]` for *every* aggregation, including `count`.
323	
324	Every matching registered series is returned on the full time grid even when
325	all of its windows are empty; no matching series yields an empty `series`
326	array. The Python per-series rows keep `series_id`; HTTP and CLI keep the
327	existing result shape. With `group_by`, all raw samples of the group's series
328	that fall in each window are pooled before aggregating (samples sharing a
329	timestamp across series count individually, `avg` divides by the total sample
330	count), a missing group key and an empty-string value stay distinct groups,
331	and each group keeps the full grid, fully null when no sample ever falls in a
332	window. Group filtering, ordering and validation follow the ordinary grouped
333	rules. The whole query reads one coherent snapshot, so concurrent writes or
334	retention sweeps can never mix old and new data; queries never alter samples,
335	counters or configuration, and the same history gives identical results after
336	reopening the store. Omitting `window_ms` preserves the previous query
337	behaviour exactly — `rollup`, write idempotency/overwrite, quotas, alerts and
338	SLOs are unaffected.
339	
340	**Counter aggregates.** In sliding-window mode `agg` also accepts `increase`
341	and `rate` (query entries only — `rollup`, alert rules and SLOs still reject
342	them, and using them without `window_ms` fails the query). Each matching
343	series is treated as a counter: within `(t - window_ms, t]` the time-sorted
344	adjacent readings contribute their difference when non-decreasing, while a
345	drop is a counter reset contributing only the later reading; the first reading
346	contributes nothing. Only samples actually inside the window are used — no
347	boundary borrowing, interpolation or extrapolation by window length.
348	`increase` is the sum of those deltas, `rate` that sum divided by the seconds
349	between the window's first and last sample. A window with fewer than two
350	distinct sample timestamps emits `[t, null]`; unchanged readings emit `0`.
351	Grouped queries compute each series independently and sum the non-null
352	per-series results (never differencing across series); a group whose series
353	are all null at a time emits null there. Any matched sample that actually
354	falls into an output window and is negative or non-finite fails the whole
355	query (`ObsError`, HTTP `400`, CLI non-zero with a one-line JSON error);
356	samples outside every window or filtered out by labels/matchers are never
357	inspected, and parameters are validated even when no series matches.
358	
359	**Retention.** `enforce_retention(tenant, cutoff_ms)` removes every sample of
360	that tenant with `timestamp_millis < cutoff_ms` and rewrites the affected point
361	files. `stats()` returns `{"series","points","writes","tenants"}`.
362	
363	**Retention policies and runs.** `set_retention(tenant, retention_ms)`
364	persists the tenant's policy in `retention.json` (also `POST
365	/v1/retention/policies` and the CLI `retention-set`); `retention_ms` is a
366	non-negative integer or `null` (no cleanup), and `get_retention(tenant)`
367	(also `GET /v1/retention/policies` and `retention-get`) returns
368	`{"tenant","retention_ms","series","points"}` — the normalised policy plus the
369	tenant's real usage, with a `null` policy for unconfigured tenants.
370	`run_retention(now_ms, tenant=None, dry_run=False)` (also `POST
371	/v1/retention/run` and `retention-run`) applies the configured policies as of
372	the injected `now_ms` (a required non-boolean integer): with a `tenant` only
373	that tenant is processed, otherwise every configured tenant in lexicographic
374	order. For each tenant `cutoff_ms = now_ms - retention_ms` and only samples
375	with `timestamp_ms < cutoff_ms` are dropped — a sample exactly at the cutoff
376	is kept; a `null` policy reports a `null` cutoff and zero deletions. Affected
377	point files are rewritten in compacted form (one physical record per
378	timestamp, the final value winning, legacy duplicate lines collapsed), empty
379	series stay registered, and the freed points count against the tenant's quota
380	immediately. The result is `{"dry_run","tenants":[...]}` with a stable
381	tenant order and `{"tenant","cutoff_ms","dropped","affected_series",
382	"remaining_points","compacted_series"}` per tenant. The whole run is one
383	atomic step under the store lock, so concurrent queries, quota and stats reads
384	only ever see the complete state before or after it; `dry_run=true` reports
385	the same numbers without touching memory, files, quotas or the write counter.
386	Policies and sweep results survive a restart. With access control enabled,
387	reading a policy is a tenant-scoped `read`, setting a policy and running a
388	single-tenant sweep are tenant-scoped `write`s, a sweep across every
389	configured tenant is admin-only, and all of them are audited.
390	
391	**Per-tenant quotas.** `set_quota(tenant, max_series, max_points)` sets the
392	tenant-wide limits; each limit is a non-negative integer or `null` (omitted
393	fields over HTTP also mean `null`, i.e. unlimited), and `0` forbids adding any.
394	`get_quota(tenant)` returns
395	`{"tenant","max_series","max_points","series","points"}` — the configured
396	limits and the current usage in one snapshot. Configuring a quota never creates
397	a series, and an unconfigured tenant is unlimited. Limits apply to all of a
398	tenant's metrics together: `series` is the number of registered series and
399	`points` the total number of *distinct timestamps* across those series, not
400	physical point-file lines. Label order, same-value replays, overwritten points
401	and a timestamp repeated inside one batch add no occupancy.
402	
403	Every write path (`SeriesStore.write`/`write_batch`, `POST /v1/series` and
404	`/v1/series/batch`, the CLI `write`/`write-batch`) is
405	checked after the existing input validation and conflict rules, using the
406	batch's net increase: a batch is rejected (ObsError / HTTP `409` / CLI JSON
407	error with non-zero exit) when *either* dimension it increases would exceed its
408	limit, and the rejection leaves no new series, samples or write-count change.
409	Limits may be lowered below current usage; afterwards only the dimensions a
410	write actually increases are checked — an already-over-limit dimension blocks
411	nothing by itself, so pure duplicates and overwrites keep succeeding. Retention
412	frees the occupancy of deleted points, while empty series stay registered.
413	Overwrites rewrite the point file so one timestamp never occupies two lines; on
414	reopen, any duplicate timestamp lines (including those left by older builds)
415	collapse to the last value, so historical re-overwrites never double-count.
416	
417	**Rule shape.** `{"id","tenant","metric","labels","comparator" ∈ {">",">=","<",
418	"<=","==","!="},"threshold","for_ms","window_ms","agg","severity" ∈ {"info",
419	"warning","critical"},"annotations"}`. `add_rule` validates every field and
420	raises `ObsError` for anything malformed (`id` is generated when omitted).
421	
422	**Evaluation window.** Let `step = window_ms`, `t = now_ms` and
423	`bucket_start(t) = t - (t % step)`. The window is
424	`[bucket_start(t) - step, t]`, i.e. the current bucket plus the whole previous
425	bucket. The rule condition holds for a series when *every* non-empty bucket in
426	that window satisfies `comparator(value, threshold)` — one violating bucket
427	anywhere in the window stops the condition, and it keeps stopping it until that
428	bucket has left the window.
429	
430	**`for_ms`.** Let `run_start` be the timestamp of the first bucket of the
431	current unbroken run of satisfying buckets (a violating bucket resets the run).
432	The rule fires only when the condition holds *and*
433	`bucket_start(now_ms) - run_start >= for_ms`. With `for_ms = 0`, one satisfied
434	bucket is enough; with `for_ms = window_ms`, the current and the previous bucket
435	must both be satisfied. Before the hold time is reached the alert is recorded
436	with `firing = false` and appears in none of the four output lists.
437	
438	**Alert identity and dedup.** Alert identity is `(rule_id, series_id)`, distinct
439	from the alert id. The first time a condition holds an alert id
440	`alert-NNNNN` is minted for that identity and reused forever: re-evaluating an
441	unchanged condition returns the *same* `id` and increments `occurrences` (the
442	number of evaluations in which the condition held). `since_ms` is `run_start`,
443	not the evaluation time, so dedup does not depend on the wall clock.
444	
445	**Resolution.** When the condition stops holding, the alert's state becomes
446	`resolved`, `firing` becomes `false`, `resolved_ms` is set once, and the alert is
447	reported in the `resolved` list of that evaluation. If the same condition holds
448	again later, the *same alert id* is reused and `occurrences` keeps counting.
449	Because the condition covers the whole window, a series that produced one bad
450	bucket stays unresolved until that bucket has left the window.
451	
452	**Silence vs inhibition precedence.** A condition that holds and whose `for_ms`
453	is satisfied is first checked against active silences: a silence is active when
454	`starts_ms <= now_ms <= ends_ms`, the tenant matches and every silence label
455	matcher is present in the series labels. Inside an active silence the alert state
456	is `silenced` (it is *not* firing) and the silence id and reason are recorded.
457	Only if no silence matches is inhibition checked: an inhibition
458	`(source_severity, target_severity, same_labels)` marks a `target_severity` alert
459	as `inhibited` while an alert of at least `source_severity` is currently
460	`firing` in the same tenant with *exactly the same label set*. Silence therefore
461	wins over inhibition. A silenced or inhibited alert still counts its
462	`occurrences` and returns to `firing` as soon as the silence/inhibition no longer
463	applies. `list_alerts(state=None)` filters by `firing`, `silenced`, `inhibited`
464	or `resolved`.
465	
466	**Notification routing.** `add_route({"tenant","target","labels"?,"severities"?,
467	"events"?,"repeat_ms"?,"id"?})` registers a notification route; `tenant` and
468	`target` are required non-empty strings, `labels` is an exact label subset the
469	alert's series must contain, `severities` (default: all severities) and
470	`events` (default: `["firing","resolved"]`, the only two allowed values) are
471	non-empty arrays when given, and `repeat_ms` is `null` or a non-negative
472	integer. Invalid shapes raise `ObsError` (HTTP `400`), a duplicate `id` is a
473	conflict (HTTP `409`), an unknown route is `404`; without an `id` the route is
474	named `route-NNNN`. Deleting a route keeps its historical notifications.
475	
476	`evaluate(now_ms)` still returns only the four state lists, but every alert
477	transition also appends to the notification queue of each matching route
478	(tenant equal, route labels a subset of the series labels, alert severity in
479	`severities`): an alert that enters `firing` — the first time, or when
480	recovering from `silenced`/`inhibited` — produces one `firing` record; while
481	the same firing state continues a repeat is emitted only when `repeat_ms` is
482	set and that much time has passed since the route's last notification for the
483	alert; entering `resolved` produces exactly one `resolved` record. Pending
484	(`for_ms` not yet met), silenced and inhibited alerts never produce `firing`
485	records. Dedup is tracked per route, so routes notify independently. Each
486	record is `{"id": "notification-NNNNN","route_id","alert_id","tenant",
487	"target","event","created_ms","alert": <snapshot>,"acked": false}` and is
488	persisted across restarts together with the dedup state.
489	`list_notifications(tenant, route_id, alert_id, acked)` reads the queue
490	without consuming it; `ack_notification(id)` marks a record acknowledged,
491	returns the same record on a repeated ack and raises `ObsError` (HTTP `404`)
492	for an unknown id.
493	
494	**SLO and error budget.** `set_slo(tenant, name, metric, labels,
495	good_comparator, threshold, target_ratio, window_ms)` defines a good-events
496	ratio SLO. `slo_status(name, now_ms, tenant=None)` counts every stored sample of
497	the matching series inside `[now_ms - window_ms, now_ms]`:
498	
499	```
500	total          = number of samples in the window (nulls excluded)
501	good           = samples where compare(value, good_comparator, threshold)
502	bad            = total - good
503	ratio          = good / total                             (0.0 when total == 0)
504	error_budget   = max(0.0, 1 - (1 - ratio) / (1 - target_ratio))   (target_ratio < 1)
505	               = 1.0 if ratio >= 1.0 else 0.0              (target_ratio == 1)
506	burn_rate      = (bad / total) / (1 - target_ratio)        (0.0 when target_ratio >= 1 or total == 0)
507	met            = ratio >= target_ratio
508	```
509	
510	`ratio` is the observed good ratio, `target_ratio ∈ (0,1]` the objective,
511	`burn_rate` how fast the budget is being spent relative to the allowed bad rate
512	(`1.0` means exactly on budget, `> 1.0` means burning too fast) and
513	`error_budget` the *fraction of the allowed error budget still unspent*:
514	`1.0` means untouched, `0.0` means exhausted or exceeded. For any `ratio` that
515	meets the target the two written forms of `error_budget` are identical, since
516	`1 - (1-ratio)/(1-target) = (ratio - target)/(1 - target)` and
517	`1 - ratio/target = (target - ratio)/target` are both non-negative only inside
518	their own regime; the first form is the one used, because it degrades sensibly
519	when the ratio beats the target (more budget left) instead of pinning to `0`.
520	With `total == 0` the ratio is `0.0`, so the budget counts as exhausted.
521	
522	Examples: 9 good + 1 bad with `target_ratio = 0.9` gives `ratio = 0.9`,
523	`error_budget = 0.0`, `burn_rate = 0.1/0.1 = 1.0`, `met = true` (exactly on
524	budget). 98 good + 2 bad with `target_ratio = 0.95` gives `ratio = 0.98`,
525	`burn_rate = 0.02/0.05 = 0.4` and `error_budget = 1 - 0.02/0.05 = 0.6` (60% of
526	the budget still unspent). 90 good + 10 bad with `target_ratio = 0.99` gives
527	`ratio = 0.9`, `burn_rate = 10.0`, `error_budget = 0.0`, `met = false`.
528	
529	**Revisions and read consistency.** The store keeps one persistent,
530	monotonically increasing *revision* in `revision.json`. Every successful
531	commit that changes samples or the visible scope — a single write, a batch
532	write, a snapshot replay or a retention run that actually drops samples —
533	increases it exactly once. Pure duplicates, dry runs, validation failures,
534	conflicts, quota rejections and retention runs that delete nothing do not
535	move it, and neither do queries, exports or SLO status reads. The counter is
536	reloaded on construction (and folded in from disk on demand), so numbering
537	continues across restarts and stays monotonic when several instances share
538	one data dir; a failed batch or replay leaves neither data nor a revision
539	trace, and concurrent queries and retention sweeps only ever see the
540	complete state before or after a commit.
541	
542	`consistency_token(tenant)` (also `GET /v1/consistency-token?tenant=` and
543	the CLI `consistency-token`) returns `{"tenant", "token", "revision"}`: an
544	HMAC-signed cursor binding the tenant to the current revision. The signing
545	secret is persisted in `revision.json`, so tokens stay verifiable after a
546	restart and across instances of the same data dir.
547	
548	The write paths accept an optional `return_revision` flag (`return_revision`
549	in the HTTP bodies, `--return-revision` on the CLI `write`, `write-batch`,
550	`replay` and `retention-run`). It must be a real boolean — an explicit
551	`null` or any other type is rejected with `400` semantics before anything
552	changes. When enabled, the result (Python dict, HTTP JSON or CLI one-line
553	JSON) carries an extra `revision`: the commit revision when the call
554	committed, otherwise the current revision. When omitted, results keep their
555	previous shape exactly.
556	
557	`query`, `export_snapshot` and `slo_status` accept an optional `read_token`
558	(`read_token` on `GET /v1/query`, `/v1/export` and `/v1/slos/status`,
559	`--read-token` on the CLI). A read carrying a token is gated on the token's
560	revision: it is processed only once this instance has caught up to it, and
561	then runs on one coherent snapshot. Re-reading with the same token may see
562	newer data but never older. A tampered, malformed, foreign or cross-tenant
563	token fails with `invalid read token` (`400`); a token whose revision the
564	instance has not reached yet fails with `read revision unavailable` (`409`).
565	The consistency-token endpoint is an ordinary tenant-scoped read: with
566	access control enabled only a principal covering the tenant can mint or use
567	its tokens, and every request is audited as usual; while no `access.json`
568	exists everything stays anonymous.
569	
570	**Determinism.** No module calls `time.time()` inside decision logic: `now_ms` is
571	passed into `evaluate`, `slo_status` and `write` (the HTTP layer uses the wall
572	clock only when a caller omits `now_ms` on `GET /v1/slos/status`, and
573	`/v1/slos/status` requires it in the CLI).
574	
575	## Layout
576	
577	```
578	obsd/__init__.py    public exports
579	obsd/tsdb.py        SeriesStore
580	obsd/alerts.py      AlertEngine
581	obsd/access.py      AccessControl (principals + audit log)
582	obsd/http_app.py    ThreadingHTTPServer + create_server
583	obsd/cli.py         command line interface
584	obsd/__main__.py    python3 -m obsd entry point
585	tests/              unittest suite (tsdb, alerts, http, access)
586	```
587	
588	## Tests
589	
590	```bash
591	python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
592	```
593	
594	Covered: series identity and label-order independence, idempotent re-write,
595	conflicting-timestamp rejection and `overwrite`, range filtering, epoch-aligned
596	buckets, null buckets, all five aggregations, deterministic rollups,
597	sliding-window grids with left-open/right-closed windows, null empty windows
598	(including count), full grids for empty series and groups, window argument
599	validation across Python/HTTP/CLI, window snapshot consistency under
600	concurrent writes and retention, retention,
601	restart safety, rule validation, `for_ms` timing, dedup with occurrence
602	counting, resolution and re-firing (including the window that keeps a bad bucket
603	blocking), silence scoping and expiry, inhibition by severity and exact label
604	set, SLO/error-budget/burn-rate math (including the empty window), quota
605	configuration/validation, net-increase enforcement and whole-batch rejection,
606	zero/lowered limits with duplicates and overwrites, tenant isolation, quota
607	release under retention, quota/usage consistency after reopen (including
608	collapsed duplicate timestamp lines), concurrent writes/reconfiguration/pruning,
609	retention policy set/get/validation and persistence, retention runs (exclusive
610	cutoff with the boundary point kept, lexicographic all-tenant sweeps, null
611	policies, dry runs without side effects, physical compaction of duplicate
612	timestamps, empty series staying registered, freed points reusable under quota,
613	restart-stable results, whole-state visibility under concurrent reads, and the
614	HTTP/CLI surfaces with tenant-scoped and admin-only access plus audit),
615	atomic multi-series batches (cross-tenant/cross-metric entries, in-batch
616	duplicate/overwrite ordering, all-or-nothing rejection on disk, per-tenant net
617	quota accounting, single write-count increment, and the HTTP/CLI surfaces),
618	principal create/list/revoke with digest-only token persistence, role and
619	tenant-scope enforcement (`401`/`403`) with the anonymous surface unchanged
620	while access control is off, per-entry batch authorization with atomic
621	rejection, the persistent audit log (seq monotonic across restarts, filters
622	and `limit` pagination on `GET /v1/audit`),
623	verifiable snapshot export (filters, ordering, digest, side-effect-free
624	repeatability across restarts) and replay (roundtrip migration, duplicate and
625	missing-point re-judgement, dry runs, digest/validation/conflict/quota
626	rejection without a trace, per-entry authorization, and the HTTP/CLI
627	surfaces),
628	the persistent revision (single increments per committing write/batch/replay/
629	retention run, no movement on duplicates, dry runs, rejections or reads,
630	restart and multi-instance continuity) with `return_revision` on every write
631	path, and read-consistency tokens (minting, tamper/cross-tenant/foreign
632	rejection, unavailable-revision `409`s, monotonic re-reads, restart
633	verifiability, and the HTTP/CLI surfaces with access control and audit),
634	and the live HTTP surface over a real socket.
635	
636	Everything is deterministic: the suite injects every timestamp it uses, and the
637	modules never read the wall clock inside decision logic.
638
